Verdict

No confirmed indicators of a malicious supply-chain compromise were found. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • No evidence was found for .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py install hooks, PEP 517 build hooks, or interpreter-startup execution in the provided code.
  • if __name__ == "__main__": main(sys.argv[1:]) in acme_tiny.py is a normal CLI path that only runs when the user directly invokes the script.
  • Even if a console_scripts entry point exists, it requires user invocation and is not, by itself, evidence of malicious automatic execution based on the current input.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** No broad collection of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets was identified. --account-key is the package’s documented ACME account-key input.
  • **Exfiltration / staging:** No evidence was found of attacker-controlled uploads, webhooks, raw-IP C2, paste/drop services, or archive staging of harvested files.
  • **Persistence:** The README crontab example appears to be user-facing documentation for certificate renewal. There is no evidence that the package creates cron jobs, systemd units, or launch agents during installation.
  • **CI/cloud lateral movement:** The GitHub Actions use of GITHUB_TOKEN and Coveralls tokens appears to be ordinary coverage-upload CI configuration. No token theft or workflow-injection behavior was identified.
  • **Obfuscation / loader:** base64 usage is consistent with ACME/JWS encoding. No eval/exec, obfuscated payload, downloader stub, platform-specific loader, or self-deleting dropper was identified.
  • **External download references:** The gist.githubusercontent.com reference in the README is documentation for a legacy Let’s Encrypt JWK key conversion script, not an automatic install/import-time download. The GitHub Actions Pebble download appears to be for test ACME server setup.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The extracted archive includes .github/workflows and .gitignore, but these are common source-distribution development/CI files and are not evidence of a malicious payload by themselves.
  • No unexplained native binaries, hidden executable payloads, sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting evidence, or wheel/sdist mismatch evidence was identified from the current input.

Further Verification Needed

  • The full text of pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and acme_tiny.egg-info/entry_points.txt was not included in the provided text corpus, so build-backend and entry-point details could not be fully verified.
  • No file-level diff against the upstream repository tag was provided; a separate comparison between the PyPI sdist and the source repository is needed to confirm artifact/source consistency.
